newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's troubled futures bourse seeks more time.
newsitem.headline: Manila's troubled futures bourse seeks more time.

text.p: The Manila International Futures Exchange (MIFE) on Tuesday asked the Securities and Exchange commission for a two-month extension before it issues the final verdict on its future.
Trading at the MIFE has been suspended since June last year due to reports of widespread irregularities.
This would give the MIFE more time to institute the reforms the SEC had required the exchange to complete before it could resume operations, MIFE said in a position paper submitted to the SEC.

These included the management of the exchange through professional managers and reducing the present number of seats at the exchange to 50 from 76 to ensure that only active, qualified members will be accepted.
It said a new futures exchange may be formed with the Philippine Stock Exchange, the Bankers Associaiton of the Philippines and a host of commodity and futures traders.

"The body agreed to pursue this plan aggressively so that the exchange could change its dimension of credibility in the business community and prove to the SEC that it really is endeavouring with unrelenting efforts to cleanse its ranks and restore its pristine credibility," MIFE said.
The exchange traded contracts in copra, sugar, dry cocoon, soybeans, coffee and major currencies. Trading volumes at the MIFE were very low. The exchange had less than 10 brokers.
